title: Westshore Bank - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
summary: Initial discovery focused on data residency, logging restrictions for financial data, and compliance (GDPR, SOC 2, HIPAA considerations for certain product lines). Westshore is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment; primary concerns are EU data residency for personal data, audit logs accessibility, and strict log redaction/retention policies. Agreed next steps: share SOC2/ISO docs, provide architecture notes for Private deployment, schedule a pilot and a technical deep-dive with infra team.
topics: Logging, audit trails, and retention policies
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
SAML/SSO, RBAC, and audit log access
action_items: Avery Martinez - Send SOC2 + ISO docs and security whitepaper - due 2026-03-27
Jordan Li - Draft Private deployment architecture note (VPC peering, KMS integration) - due 2026-04-01
Maya Singh - Share list of data flows and locations (which workloads require EU residency) - due 2026-03-30
Ethan Cole - Confirm stakeholders for pilot and preferred timeline - due 2026-03-29
next_steps: Share security/compliance pack (SOC2, ISO, privacy datasheet)
Schedule SE-led technical deep dive for April 2nd (infra + networking)
Setup pilot scope doc and proposed timeline (2-4 weeks)
Provide preliminary pricing for Dedicated and Private options
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-25 15:00 EDT | Duration: ~46 mins | Attendees: Avery, Jordan (Redwood) / Daniel, Maya, Ethan (Westshore)

[00:00] Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, um let's do quick intros i think we have, uh, about 45 minutes. Avery Martinez here from Redwood, i'm the account.. uh account exec.
[00:12] Daniel: hi, daniel park, ciso at westshore bank. thanks for taking the time.
[00:16] Maya: maya singh, head of devops. i'll be focused on networking and infra constraints.
[00:21] Ethan: ethan cole, product, i'll talk roadmap and use-cases.
[00:24] Jordan: jordan li, systems engineer on the inference side, i'll cover architecture.
[00:29] Avery: great, quick agenda, we want to understand your compliance reqs (gdpr, soc2, any hipaa overlap), data residency needs (eu/us), logging retention and redaction, and then map to hosted/dedicated/private options.
[00:45] Daniel: yes the big ones: gdpr for any eu customers, SOC 2 is required, and some of our lines (we have a health benefits product) might touch PHI so we need to understand hipaa posture too. also, we have very strict logging policies, we can't store PII in logs beyond X days and access to audit logs has to be restricted.
[01:10] Avery: understood. high level, Redwood Hosted keeps data in region-backed clusters, we offer regional tenancy for EU and US, but for highest control you can use Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Redwood Private which is VPC or on-prem and gives customer-managed networking and KMS.
[01:30] Maya: right, so question: if we go hosted, is there a guarantee that EU data stays in eu? and where are the logs stored, cause our compliance team will want to control retention.
[01:40] Jordan: for Hosted we map region to cloud region, so e.g. eu-west-1 hosts EU traffic. there are caveats around backups, async logs, and third-party integrations; we can toggle retention and redact at ingest for many fields, but for strictest control we recommend Dedicated or Private where logs can live in your VPC or be forwarded to your splunk/s3 with lifecycle policies.
[02:05] Daniel: when you say redact at ingest, is that deterministic? we need to guarantee no PII fields in logs — names, ssn, account numbers — basically anything sensitive. we also have e-discovery / audit readiness requirements.
[02:20] Jordan: currently we have configurable redaction rules and tokenization; for e2e guarantee we typically recommend customer-side pre-processing or Private deployment with no logging of raw prompts. we also support automatic PII detection heuristics but it's not 100% foolproof — you know, transcription models sometimes miss.
[02:42] Ethan: so operationally, if we do Private on our VPC, what's the integration with our KMS? we use aws-kms with external key policies.
[02:50] Jordan: Private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations; we can do BYOK (bring your own key) so keys never leave your control. with Dedicated we also offer KMS integrations but logs and some control plane telemetry might still be in Redwood-managed infra unless we set up private control plane.
[03:10] Maya: how about SSO and RBAC? we need SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC tied to AD groups, and audit logs that show who queried what model when.
[03:20] Avery: yes we have SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning and RBAC. Redwood Console surfaces per-user audit trails; for Private, those logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. note: some attributes like model internals are not exposed but request-level metadata is.
[03:40] Daniel: GDPR question: if a eu subject asks for deletion, how do we handle model inputs that have been used to train or fine-tune models — is that a risk?
[03:50] Jordan: Redwood doesn't train customer data into shared models; for Hosted we have strong guarantees about data usage, we don't use customer prompts for model training unless opted in. for Dedicated and Private, by default data stays isolated. for full erasure, we can purge logs and cached prefixes, but removing "learned" behavior from a large model is non-trivial — usually we avoid that by not using customer data for training.
[04:20] Maya: ok but still need a written attestation for gdpr and data processing addendum.
[04:25] Avery: absolutely we'll send our DPA and privacy datasheet.
[04:30] Ethan: what's the approach to latency vs cost — if we need strict residency and low latency, seems like dedicated or private is expensive. any recommendations?
[04:40] Jordan: tradeoff: Hosted is cheapest and fastest to start, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale, and Private gives max isolation but higher ops cost. we recommend starting with Dedicated for production spike and then a Private pilot if compliance requires it. Redwood Optimize can give quantization and batching recs to reduce cost while keeping latency SLOs.
[05:05] Daniel: auditability: we need immutable audit logs for 7 years for certain transactions — can Redwood support that?
[05:13] Jordan: yes we can forward logs to customer S3 or SIEM with WORM policies, or we can retain in-service with configurable retention. for the Hosted plan we have retention options but long-tail retention might require an add-on.
[05:30] Maya: network egress — if we do Private VPC in our AWS account, will there be any egress to Redwood control plane that could leak data?
[05:38] Jordan: Private has two models: private control plane (we install a control-plane connector in your VPC so metadata stays internal) vs managed control plane (some telemetry to Redwood). for highest assurance we do private control plane so only billing/alerts flow out minimal encrypted metadata. we'll detail this in the architecture note.
[06:00] Ethan: there's also procurement reading — we need sample contracts and timelines for Dedicated vs Private procurement and compliance review.
[06:08] Avery: sure, i'll include sample language and typical timelines — Dedicated procurement ~4-8 weeks, Private can be 8-16+ depending on legal and network set up.
[06:20] Daniel: HIPAA: even though we don't handle clinical records, our benefits product might. do you sign BAAs?
[06:28] Avery: we do sign BAAs for customers with covered workloads; we'll pass you the BAA template.
[06:33] Maya: curious about model variants and fallback — if an EU region goes down, will traffic route to us-east and thus expose eu data in the us?
[06:43] Jordan: by default our routing prefers region; for Hosted we have automatic fallback but you can disable cross-region failover for strictly geo-restricted data. with Private and Dedicated you control routing policies.
[06:58] Ethan: any tooling for masking user inputs before they hit the model?
[07:03] Jordan: we have a client-side SDK with pre-processing hooks and a gateway option to do PII masking, plus server-side redaction. for highest assurance we recommend both.
[07:16] Daniel: ok, external auditors will also want to see encryption in transit and at rest proofs, and key rotation logs.
[07:23] Jordan: we have TLS 1.2/1.3, at-rest encryption on disks, and KMS logs can be forwarded to your CloudTrail. key rotation can be customer-controlled for BYOK.
[07:36] Avery: any constraints on data residency for non-personal telemetry? like usage metrics?
[07:42] Maya: devops wants some telemetry aggregated in us for operations, but compliance only cares about PII.
[07:48] Jordan: we can partition telemetry — customer-visible product telemetry can be sent to your metrics pipeline, and we can anonymize or aggregate before leaving region. we'll include examples.
[08:05] Daniel: about logging retention window — we have to purge certain logs after 30 days but keep audit trails for 7 years. sounds conflicting.
[08:13] Jordan: yes typical pattern: redact PII quickly (30 days), retain stripped audit metadata long-term (7 years). we can implement field-level lifecycle.
[08:25] Ethan: what's the SLA for Dedicated and Private?
[08:29] Avery: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets (we'll send the SLA doc). Private depends on deployment model; with private control plane and dedicated infra we can offer enterprise SLA in contract.
[08:42] Maya: networking specifics — we'll need firewall rules and peering docs for our security team, and a list of egress IPs if any.
[08:50] Jordan: we'll provide a network runbook and IP ranges; for Private, egress is your VPC so you control it.
[09:02] Daniel: curious about data deletion workflow: if a user asks for deletion, how quickly can we purge cached KV prefixes, logs, and backups?
[09:11] Jordan: we can purge active caches within minutes, logs per retention policy, backups depend on backup lifecycle but we can do expedited purge for compliance in coordination with ops. we'll note RTO/RPO expectations.
[09:30] Avery: any other regulatory exposures? do you have EU subsidiaries that need data residency in EU only?
[09:36] Daniel: yes we have EU customers primarily for our retail banking product, so those prompts must stay in eu region.
[09:42] Jordan: ok so recommended: EU-dedicated endpoint or Private deployment in eu region with private control plane.
[09:51] Ethan: cost ask — can you give us ballpark monthly for Dedicated for our expected throughput?
[09:56] Avery: we'll do a sizing call, but ballpark depends on concurrent requests and token volume — i'll follow up with pricing scenarios in the pilot doc.
[10:05] Maya: would we be able to run a POC that runs synthetic traffic to measure latency to our EU users?
[10:10] Jordan: yes we can run benchmarks from eu endpoints and share tail latency metrics; we also have perf harnesses we can run in your account for Private.
[10:20] Daniel: curious if Redwood collects any raw prompts in Hosted for telemetry — you said earlier not for training, but do you store them for debug a window?
[10:28] Jordan: short-term debug logs may persist but are access-restricted and can be disabled; for full compliance we can turn off raw prompt retention and only keep metadata. we'll indicate retention windows in the security docs.
[10:45] Avery: let's recap and next steps. we'll send SOC2/ISO, DPA, BAA template, private architecture note, network runbook, and preliminary pricing. schedule a technical deep-dive April 2nd.
[10:58] Ethan: sounds good. i'll loop in procurement and legal after we get the docs.
[11:05] Daniel: one more — do you support on-prem airgapped deployments?
[11:09] Jordan: yes we offer an on-prem package for air-gapped envs; it's typically heavier lift but available for regulated workloads.
[11:18] Maya: ok i'll prepare a list of stakeholders and dataflow diagrams for the next call.
[11:23] Avery: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll send notes and action items.
[11:27] (end)

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts — product names sometimes mis-spelled (e.g., "Redwood Consle"), proper nouns may be rough. Shared artifacts referenced: security pack link: https://redwood.docs/security-pack.zip ; private arch note (placeholder): https://redwood.docs/private-arch.pdf ; sample sla and dpa: https://redwood.docs/legal/sla-dpa.zip
questions: Can hosting guarantee EU-only residency and disable cross-region failover?
Do you sign BAAs for HIPAA-covered workloads?
Can audit logs be forwarded to our SIEM with WORM retention?
Is BYOK with AWS KMS supported in Private deployments?
